1 │ # The message I get when I try to change a frozen object is shared and not my own
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ When I try to change a value on an object that was made frozen, the error text is
   6 │ stored just once on the error type itself. Every error of that kind points at the
   7 │ same, changeable list of words instead of carrying its own message. Because it is a
   8 │ list, someone can change it in one place and every error in the whole program shows
   9 │ the changed words. So when I catch the error, reading the message off it is not
  10 │ dependable, and matching that text is not dependable either.
  11 │ 
  12 │ ## What should happen
  13 │ 
  14 │ After the change, each error raised when I try to change a frozen object carries its
  15 │ own fixed copy of the text. The words I read off the caught error are the same words
  16 │ as its first argument, and they say that the attribute cannot be set. Each error
  17 │ stands on its own, so changing one can never change any other. I can catch the error
  18 │ and read or match its message without surprises.
  19 │ 
  20 │ ## About this project
  21 │ 
  22 │ This project is a library called attrs. It helps people build classes that hold data,
  23 │ with much less typing than writing them by hand. One of its features is "frozen",
  24 │ which locks an object after it is created so nobody can change it afterwards. When
  25 │ someone does try to change a frozen object, the library raises an error that explains
  26 │ what went wrong.
  27 │ 
  28 │ ## Problem this solves
  29 │ 
  30 │ People who catch the error from changing a frozen object cannot trust the message
  31 │ they get, because the same text is shared by every error and can be changed in one
  32 │ place. They need the text on each caught error to belong to that error alone, so
  33 │ reading it or matching it always gives the same, correct answer.
  34 │ 
  35 │ ## What changed
  36 │ 
  37 │ The error raised when changing a frozen object now sets its own message when it is
  38 │ created. The message on the caught error equals its first argument and says that the
  39 │ attribute cannot be set. The old shared, changeable list of words is gone, so one
  40 │ error can no longer affect the message seen on another. Everything else about how
  41 │ frozen objects behave stays the same.
  42 │ 
  43 │ ## Impact
  44 │ 
  45 │ Correctness and ease of use when handling errors from frozen objects.
  46 │ 
  47 │ ## User experience
  48 │ 
  49 │ Before: I change a value on a frozen object, catch the error, and its message comes
  50 │ from one shared, changeable list, so the text is not reliably mine. After: I change a
  51 │ value on a frozen object, catch the error, and it shows its own fixed message saying
  52 │ the attribute cannot be set, and that same text is its first argument.
  53 │
